summary: BG2 podcast (May 2025): Gerstner and Gurley discuss the Gulf AI deals and repeal of the AI diffusion rule, the US-China tariff truce and market rebound, the reconciliation bill and deficit, Delaware corporate law, stablecoin legislation and Chinese open-source models. Mostly policy/venture commentary with a few macro points: blended tariff math (~$300B on $28T GDP is a modest headwind), tax-bill stimulus size, deficit scoring caveats.

coverage.note: Intro: Google analogy, market bounce after tariff/Middle East news, Middle East trip, diffusion rule repeal
Trillion-dollar Gulf investment pledges, UAE 5GW AI campus, Huawei/Chinese stack risk in Gulf
Gulf competitive advantages: cheap power, power share of token COGS, latency, labor
Framework not one-off; wall around America vs open diffusion; Europe regulation; decelerationists
American AI stack argument; Iran/Syria/Abraham Accords outlook; China hawk industrial complex and VC bias
Disagreement on China; market catalyst was US-China tariff deal; Navarro vs Bessent paths; chaos cost
China tariff structure; blended tariff math ($300B vs $800B); market bounce rationale
Rare earth pause; H20 ban and Nvidia China sales; China already has frontier AI; export controls backfire
Reconciliation bill mechanics; tax cut extension, expensing, stimulus size
Big six negotiators; CBO scoring, deficit and debt, tariff revenue and DOGE not counted; military budget cuts
Defense budget; balanced budget and growth; monetizing land; sovereign wealth fund; debt burden
Carried interest/tax hikes; Laffer curve; Invest America design
Invest America in House bill and MAGA-account naming; Delaware chancery firestorm
Grundfest study of Delaware fee multiples; two judges; assignment power
Delaware risk; Tesla nine-share plaintiff; Texas SB29 provisions
Texas/Nevada competition; Delaware inertia; Hester Peirce crypto paper; public company count
GENIUS Act stablecoin legislation; reserves; stablecoin demand for Treasuries; payments friction; tokenization
Crypto regulatory stall; Baidu open-sourcing, four Chinese open models; US open-source outlook
Open models used to train proprietary; Manus facts; Chinese AI researchers share
Skilled immigration, reciprocity, selective engagement with China, sign-off

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: The market which was down 20% for the year has now bounced 20% in the last uh 20 trading days.
claims.claim: US equities fully recovered an early-2025 20% drawdown within 20 trading days as tariffs de-escalated and deals were announced.
claims.indicator: US equity index drawdown and rebound (Apr-May 2025)

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it broadly restricted the ability of the US to sell chips to like a 100 countries around the world
claims.claim: The Biden diffusion rule restricted US chip and model exports to about 100 countries; its repeal opens large AI-infrastructure demand for US suppliers.
claims.indicator: US export controls on advanced AI chips
claims.testable: partly: event study of chip stocks

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we would have gotten a trillion dollar deal signed with Saudi in terms of their investment in the United States
claims.claim: Gulf sovereigns (Saudi, Qatar, UAE) pledged roughly $1 trillion each in US investment in early 2025, supporting US capital inflows and AI buildout.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: 5 gigs every gig is about 500,000 GPUs
claims.claim: The UAE-US 5 GW AI campus equals about 2.5 million GPUs of compute, a measure of AI capex scale.
claims.indicator: GW of compute; GPUs per GW

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: It was basically going to allow for this Huawei belt and road where Chinese full stack technologies would would would move into the Middle East.
claims.claim: Restricting US AI exports pushes allies toward Chinese full-stack technology, reducing long-run US tech dominance.
claims.direction: Huawei share up if US restricts

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: A primitive to to AI is power and they have cheap power
claims.claim: Cheap energy (solar, nuclear, gas) gives Gulf states a cost advantage in producing AI tokens, since AI is effectively converting electrons into tokens.
claims.indicator: cost of power for data centers

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: a two to one power advantage, you might pick up five percentage points of operating margin
claims.claim: Power and cooling are only about 15-20% of COGS, so a 2x power advantage is worth only about five points of margin, a smaller edge than often assumed.
claims.indicator: power share of data-center COGS (about 10% of revenue)
claims.testable: yes: rough estimate flagged as uncertain

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: you just have the issue of latency, right? So uh this part of the world needs uh local data centers
claims.claim: Latency and proximity create demand for local data centers in Europe, the Middle East and India beyond power cost.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: we were going to have a wall around America and there was going to be America AI and then China AI was going to have the rest of the world
claims.claim: Export restrictions would repeat the internet pattern in reverse, with US AI walled off and Chinese AI serving the rest of the world.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: complex reg regulations have have limited or stifled innovation
claims.claim: A WSJ article shows Europe lags in business culture and tech because complex regulation stifles innovation on labor and technology; US policies under consideration mirrored these.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we are not only safer, we are more prosperous when the world runs on the American AI stack
claims.claim: US benefits economically and strategically when the world's AI runs on American technology; thus diffusion favours Nvidia, AMD and OpenAI.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the president's lifting of the sanctions on Syria probably gives way uh to uh the Saudis signing the Abraham Accords
claims.claim: Sanctions relief on Syria may lead to Saudi joining the Abraham Accords, while Iran is at a fork between a nuclear deal and a hot war.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: It's like defend defending your children, once you invest in something, you just start to adopt the uh the mouthpiece for it
claims.claim: Investors in defense and military-linked companies tend to adopt China-hawk positions to support their holdings, so such opinions are biased by position.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: you had the walking back of tariffs on China
claims.claim: The US-China tariff truce in Switzerland, more than the Gulf deals, was the catalyst for the market rebound.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: Because we knew $2 trillion in tariffs is probably a 600 to 700 basis point headwind to GDP.
claims.claim: A $2 trillion tariff regime (Navarro path) would have been a 600-700 bp GDP headwind, which explains the 20% equity drop; the Bessent/Hassett path of narrow tariffs was market-friendly.
claims.indicator: size of tariff revenue relative to GDP

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: that chaos is very difficult both for investors but also for executives like committing to hiring programs committing to capex all these things
claims.claim: Policy chaos and uncertainty delay corporate hiring and capex, so reduced uncertainty is bullish.
claims.direction: capex and hiring down under uncertainty

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: if you put China at 30% on strategic, at 15% on non-strategic, and then the rest of the world roughly at 10%. You come up with about 300 billion in tariffs
claims.claim: A blended tariff scenario implies about $300 billion in tariffs versus $77 billion last year and $800 billion under the Liberation Day list.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: half of that will show up as increased prices and taxes on consumers and on businesses half of it will get eaten by the the producer of the product
claims.claim: About half of tariff costs are passed to US buyers and half absorbed by foreign producers, so $300 billion on a $28 trillion economy is a modest headwind.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we're just back to where we started the year the markets were down 20% now they're up 20%
claims.claim: The market rebound merely recovered losses once the policy path became defined.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: those restrictions were removed as part of this first 90-day pause
claims.claim: Rare earth and magnet export restrictions were removed in the 90-day pause, easing supply concerns for strategic-input users, but may return.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: I would not be terribly surprised to see Nvidia allowed to sell some form of deprecated chip into China
claims.claim: A negotiated allowance of lower-end Nvidia chips to China is plausible within 90 days; an export ban costs US tax revenue and R&D.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: China already has Frontier AI. Huawei is already there.
claims.claim: China already has frontier AI, so restrictions cannot keep it from China.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: keeping companies like Bite Dance and Tencent, etc. in the CUDA ecosystem rather than allowing all of that data
claims.claim: Selling chips to China keeps Chinese firms in the CUDA ecosystem and US profit/tax base rather than the Huawei ecosystem.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: who now believe that you know restricting our technology into China just gives them more and more incentive to implement their own technology faster
claims.claim: Technology restrictions accelerate Chinese indigenous development, as seen in autos and robotics.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: only have to get to 50 votes in the Senate rather than the 60 votes
claims.claim: Reconciliation needs only 50 Senate votes if provisions relate to the budget, so tax and budget changes can pass quickly.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: that would be a major like a three trillion4 trillion dollar increase to taxes at the end of this year unless they're extended
claims.claim: Expiry of the 2017 tax cuts would be a $3-4 trillion tax increase, so the bill extends them.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the immediate expensing of capital investment. This is huge for business.
claims.claim: Immediate tax expensing of capital equipment and software boosts business investment incentives.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: that's probably a four or$500 billion annual stimulus to the economy
claims.claim: Combined tax provisions (no tax on tips, overtime, social security, expensing) amount to a $400-500 billion annual stimulus.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: we had just had a $2.2 trillion deficit. You know, we have a $ 38 trillion debt.
claims.claim: The US ran a $2.2 trillion deficit with $38 trillion debt, and the reconciliation package will probably increase the deficit rather than cut it.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: They don't count that in the budget.
claims.claim: Tariff revenue (~$300B) is not counted in CBO budget scoring, and DOGE cuts are not counted without rescission, so official deficit math understates tariff offsets and overstates deficits.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it also will lead to much higher economic growth than we would have otherwise had
claims.claim: The Council of Economic Advisers argues tax cuts raise growth; Gerstner agrees lower taxes mean higher growth but worries about the deficit.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: Trump mentioned potentially discussing with China and Russia cutting all of our military budgets in half
claims.claim: A joint cut of military budgets would be the biggest deficit lever if geopolitical tensions calmed.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the defense department budget goes up by about $150 billion as part of this package
claims.claim: Defense spending rises about $150B to roughly $1 trillion in the package.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I would love to believe that we're going to grow our economy at four or 5% per year instead of 2% per year because that would grow our way out of the problem.
claims.claim: Growth of 4-5% would solve the debt problem but is too aggressive to forecast.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the university system here was don was granted as a gift years ago 2.1 million acres in the uh in the Perian Basin
claims.claim: Government land could be monetized, as Texas's university endowment of 2.1 million Permian acres yields about $894 million a year.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: rather than putting that money in a in a sovereign wealth fund, we're just going to use it to pay down the debt
claims.claim: Asset monetization proceeds would go to debt paydown, putting a sovereign wealth fund on the back burner.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: neither of those provisions um are in the House version of the reconciliation bill
claims.claim: Carried interest elimination and higher top tax rates are not in the House bill because Republicans oppose tax hikes.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: At some point, taxes go up to a point where your tax revenues actually go down, right?
claims.claim: Laffer-curve argument: top marginal all-in rates around 57% disincentivize work, so higher taxes may not raise revenue.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: such that by the age of 18, you could have about $50,000 in that account. At age 30, you could have about $150,000 in the account.
claims.claim: Invest America seeds each newborn with $1,000 in an S&P 500 account that compounds to about $50,000 by 18 and $150,000 by 30 with contributions.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: every company in the state of Delaware now heading for the exits
claims.claim: After the Tesla pay ruling companies considered leaving Delaware; claim of mass reincorporation.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: in Delaware um seven times or higher is 23 times more likely than in a federal court
claims.claim: Grundfest research (2009-2024) shows Delaware fee multiples of seven times or higher are 23 times and ten times or higher 57 times more frequent than in federal court, indicating governance risk.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the chancellor um who is one of the two gets to pick who the cases are assigned to
claims.claim: 55% of the highest-multiplier awards come from two judges and the chancellor assigns cases, creating concentrated unpredictable outcomes.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: in the Tesla case, the plaintiff had nine shares
claims.claim: In the Tesla case a plaintiff with nine shares generated a roughly $345-380M lawyer fee, showing misaligned litigation incentives.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: a minimum threshold of up to 3% on what's needed to bring a derivative action
claims.claim: Texas SB 29 allows a 3% shareholder threshold for derivative suits, codifies the business judgment rule and limits opportunistic claims to attract incorporation.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: 90 plus% of companies and lawyers and, you know, went back to incorporating the state of Delaware because that's just the way that momentum and inertia works
claims.claim: Inertia keeps most companies in Delaware despite the ruling.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: crypto and blockchain specifically may be a better mechanism for tracking securities
claims.claim: SEC commissioner Hester Peirce argues blockchains could better track securities and regulatory capture produces market fragility; she proposes a sandbox.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: she also brings that up the number of public companies is way down from its peak
claims.claim: The number of US public companies is far below its peak, linked to regulation and IPO inefficiency.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it requires stable coin issuers to maintain reserves equal to the value of their issued tokens
claims.claim: The GENIUS Act requires full reserve backing and gives regulatory certainty to stablecoin issuers.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: in 5 to 10 years, stable coin issuers will become the biggest holders of US debt on the planet because they have to own that debt to back
claims.claim: Stablecoin growth, since reserves must be held in Treasuries, could make issuers the largest buyers of US debt.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: People today pay ridiculous fees to move money around.
claims.claim: Stablecoin payment rails cut transaction friction, raising growth and reducing the tax burden on the economy.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the fourth deep pocketfunded model in China that are all open- source
claims.claim: Baidu joins DeepSeek, Qwen and another in Chinese open-source models, creating competitive dynamic and rapid innovation.
claims.direction: China early leadership in open source

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: different models can help improve other models. Having four simultaneous models out there all open source
claims.claim: Open models can be used to improve other models, making open-source competition hard for closed labs to match.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: you're going to see the open AI uh open- source model
claims.claim: OpenAI is expected to release an open-source model within about 30 days.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the people with proprietary models will use these to train them because they're available
claims.claim: Proprietary labs will train on available open models, so bans on DeepSeek are whack-a-mole.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: I think 50% of researchers AI researchers in the United States of America are Chinese
claims.claim: About half of US AI researchers are of Chinese background, so anti-China rhetoric risks hurting talent supply.
claims.testable: partly: the statistic is quoted second-hand

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the number one thing we could do would be to open up our border for skilled immigration from China as wide as we possibly can
claims.claim: Skilled immigration from China, such as an AI visa, would be the best US competitive move.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I'd love to see tariffs come down on both sides
claims.claim: Reciprocal tariff reduction and market opening with China benefits both; engage on non-strategic trade while competing on strategic goods.
